request.hypothesis: A two-segment serial external-tendon design with lengths 0.20 m and 0.16 m, circular sections radius 0.008 m, and three independent 120-degree-spaced tendons on each segment can realize the required first-segment bend while leaving the distal segment nearly straight. In a planar calculation, a 0.20 m first segment bent by about 0.8 rad and a straight 0.16 m distal segment produce a tip near (0.291, 0, 0.190) m; a small out-of-plane bend can supply the target -0.035 m y-coordinate. The 3-per-segment tendon spans are intended to provide independent bending authority rather than coupling both segments through a single span.
request.expected_observation: Generation returns a valid serial_family_generation_v2 candidate artifact with two segments, six tendons, accepted section/routing/clearance and parameter domains, and a capability view showing the intended segment and tendon ordering. This is expected to be a design-validity result only, not a task-acceptance or measured-reach result.
request.weakening_observation: Generation rejects the span configuration, guide/anchor stations, tendon clearance, or section domains; or the resulting candidate capability view shows a topology or tendon ordering incompatible with independent three-tendon control of each segment. Any such outcome weakens the design hypothesis and requires a structural revision before control initialization.
request.fixed_conditions: Frozen reach task identity d24aeac7041052ce1d2ae60e825a802e7367107784f6fec192b0a65c4a5e76e7, target_m [0.29, -0.035, 0.19], 0.35 s duration, 0.01 s control period, 0.05 s holding window, original sealed evaluator and thresholds remain unchanged. Family space is serial_external_tendons_s7 with generation serial_family_generation_v2 and polar_consecutive_spans_v1 routing.
request.stopping_condition: Stop this generation attempt if the candidate is rejected or invalid; otherwise stop after the generated candidate artifact is returned and proceed to explicit baseline control initialization. Do not claim reach or task acceptance from generation alone.
request.interpretation: A valid generated candidate would be only a legal structural prior. It would not establish controllability, dynamic reach, or acceptance; those require a later independent measured evaluation. Rejection would provide concrete structural feedback for revision rather than evidence of global infeasibility.

request.hypothesis: A two-segment, 0.44 m total-length, four-tendon polar-routed continuum design with 8 mm circular sections and 18 mm tendon routing radius can produce the roughly 5 rad/m bending curvature needed to bring the tip near the target (0.29, -0.035, 0.19) while respecting the declared curvature, force, clearance, and tendon domains.

request.weakening_observation: Generation is rejected, the candidate capability view shows incompatible routing or guide clearance, the effective total length is insufficient, or the declared curvature/force domains cannot realize the required bend.
request.fixed_conditions: Frozen task target and duration; family space serial_external_tendons_s7; two segments; four tendons; one polar consecutive span from segment 0 to segment 1; task grid and evaluator unchanged.
request.stopping_condition: Stop the design-generation step when a valid candidate artifact is returned, or when generation fails and the exact domain/routing rejection is available for revision; do not begin physical replay before a valid design and control seed exist.
request.interpretation: Generation is only a design proposal and establishes no measured task acceptance. A valid artifact would justify initialization and independent physical evaluation; a rejection would identify which structural domain or routing constraint must be revised.

request.hypothesis: The registered default candidate (artifact 8a73…d31d, serial_external_tendons_s7, generation v2 defaults) has enough bending authority under its declared tension limits that a model-based task_gap optimization from a cold constant-0.2 N initialization reaches a predicted post-step tip within a small multiple of the 0.01 m tolerance of the target [0.29,-0.035,0.19]; i.e. the design is not the binding limitation and the remaining gap, if any, is a control/timing problem.
request.expected_observation: A converged (or iteration-limited) SoRoSim task_gap solution whose predicted terminal tip error is on the order of 1e-3 to low 1e-2 m — small enough to be plausible under 0.01 m once controllers move faster than the cold-optimized schedule — with tensions staying inside the declared per-tendon force limits and a terminal speed low enough that the final-0.05 s holding window is not obviously hopeless.
request.weakening_observation: The reported predicted task gap stays at the order of the workspace scale (tens of mm) with saturated tensions, i.e. the optimizer cannot move the tip toward the target direction at all from this design, or it terminates on numerical/iteration limits without meaningful improvement over the constant pretension start. That would indicate the geometry/routing, not the input sequence, is binding and push toward generate (design modification).
request.fixed_conditions: Frozen task (target [0.29,-0.035,0.19], 0.35 s, 0.01 s control period, 0.0005 s timestep, 0.05 s holding window, position 0.01 m / speed 0.02 m/s limits), candidate 8a73…d31d unmodified, declared tendon force limits and pretension defaults, objective_mode task_gap, position_weight 1, speed_weight 1, secondary_coefficient 0.001, substeps 1, max_iterations 120, no warm source (none eligible).
request.stopping_condition: One mathematical evaluation is charged regardless of outcome; stop this analysis step when the mechanics run returns a predicted trajectory/task-gap summary or a numerical-failure status, and do not repeat it with the other cold initialization in this same step.
request.interpretation: If the predicted gap is small I will treat the design as a usable prior, initialize control on this candidate (baseline pretension or a response-based seed) and spend the physical budget on control search over the 0.35 s window. If the predicted gap is large despite saturated tensions, the model result weakens the design prior and I will instead modify structure via generate (segment count/length/section/stiffness) and re-check. Either way this result is a model-side, check-only prior with no task acceptance; no feasibility, optimality or robustness claim follows from it.
